measurement: native invocation attempt for the newly covered accessibility controls
result: NOT EXERCISED NATIVELY. On the initial surface only task-search was present; it exposes ValuePattern and not InvokePattern, which is expected for a text field, so the invoke threw. surface-switcher, flow-search, compare-change-a, compare-close, stop-request and stop-reconcile were absent because they belong to other surfaces, and reaching those needs navigation this session cannot deliver. The change is therefore verified by the unit tests and the Gate only, not by a native activation.
what_this_means: Adding the listener is justified by the preview-button evidence - the same defect class, fixed and measured - but for these eight controls the fix is unmeasured. No claim is made that they now respond to accessibility activation.
guard_limitation: The per-control test bounds each control by the next .id(" occurrence, which is not a reliable element boundary: compare-close's window still spans roughly seventeen thousand characters and reaches flow-node click handling, and surface-switcher is a group whose listeners sit on children in a form the boundary never sees. The test therefore demonstrates that the eight named handlers exist in production code, not that each control is bound to its own listener. A per-element binding test needs element-scoped anchors and is not done.
exclusions: Six click targets were left out, and the reasons given for them were wrong twice, so here is what the source shows. flow-diagram-region IS a real element (lib.rs:5499), not a test string. surface-switcher is a group whose per-surface listeners live on children built with .id(("surface", index)) (lib.rs:5149), so it needs its own treatment rather than a single element listener. The remaining four (candidate cards, task rows and the flow diagram nodes) carry dynamic ids and click closures that capture click keys and entity handles, so a plain Click action cannot express activation for them.
guard_fix: FIXED AND PROVEN, IN TWO PARTS. The count-based test now reads only the production half of the file (before the first #[cfg(test)] module) so its own literals cannot satisfy it, and renaming one production listener makes it fail. A second test checks each of the eight controls individually by locating its .id(...) and requiring an explicit listener within the following text, because a count cannot show that a particular control has one. Structural analysis of every .on_click remains undone.
